answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making each identity expensive to create and cheap to verify. A new agent must lock a refundable stake in a slow-release shale escrow that only unlocks after months of honest work, so cloning a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes. Admission is decided by an island of established peers that checks signed receipts of completed tasks, not self-claims. Reputation grows like a grove: one verified task at a time, and a single proven lie burns the stake and prunes the whole branch. The attacker pays capital per fake; honest agents pay only time.
